meta.purpose: The tax/compliance layer that turns a gross quote into NET CASH RECEIVED. The compass price-book examples omit this — always apply it for Egypt-touching deals.
meta.source: Service Pricing Cost Calculation (Egypt case study) + verified research report, June 2026. Figures confirmed against Law 67/2016 (VAT), Law 91/2005 (income/WHT), Law 148/2019 (social insurance), Law 152/2020 + Law 6/2025 (MSME), Law 7/2024 (PIT brackets), Law 14/2025 (labour).
meta.verify_status: Confirmed June 2026. Tax law still changes — re-confirm with a local accountant before contracting. See references/source_analysis.md.

vat.standard_rate_digital_software_3d: 14% — software, digital media, 3D animation are STANDARD-rated; input VAT fully recoverable with valid e-invoices.
vat.professional_consulting_schedule_tax: 10% schedule tax on PURE professional/consultancy/advisory services — input VAT recovery RESTRICTED. WARNING: on blended contracts (software + strategy consulting) itemize precisely or auditors may reclassify the whole deliverable under the restrictive 10% regime.
vat.exported_services_rate: 0% — remote services to a NON-resident with no physical presence in the other jurisdiction (Executive Instructions 45/2025). Input VAT FULLY recoverable -> cash-flow subsidy for export work. NOTE: local branches of foreign entities = domestic, charge 14%.
vat.e_invoicing: Mandatory; registration threshold LOWERED from EGP 500,000 to EGP 250,000 gross annual revenue (Resolution 281/2025, deadline 31 Mar 2026). Paper invoices invalid for VAT recovery / cost deduction since July 2023.
vat.reverse_charge: Egyptian buyer self-accounts 14% VAT on foreign services and reclaims as input (cash-neutral) — BUT requires an active Tax Reg Number + annually-renewable Unique ID Number (UIN) that the foreign vendor validates via ETA API (since 1 Nov 2024). If the UIN lapses, the vendor bills a hard, non-recoverable 14% B2C VAT.

withholding_tax_local.trigger: Payments by Egyptian corporates to local vendors > EGP 300.
withholding_tax_local.base: PRE-VAT (net) invoice amount, not the gross.
withholding_tax_local.filing: Quarterly, Form 41 (within 1 month of quarter-end). Payer bears absolute liability; failure = penalties + total disallowance of the expense.
withholding_tax_local.worked: Invoice EGP 100,000 + 14% VAT = 114,000 gross. 5% WHT on 100,000 = 5,000. Net cash to provider = 114,000 - 5,000 = 109,000.
withholding_tax_local.recovery: Creditable against the provider's own income tax — a cash-flow hit, not a permanent loss.

withholding_tax_crossborder.rate: 20% blanket on service fees / royalties / licenses / cloud paid by an Egyptian firm to a NON-resident.
withholding_tax_crossborder.sourcing_rule: CONFIRMED as a real blanket rate. Under Law 91/2005 'utilization' sourcing, any service CONSUMED in Egypt is Egyptian-source regardless of where performed or whether the provider has a Permanent Establishment. Services performed abroad are NOT exempt under domestic law.
withholding_tax_crossborder.correction_note: An earlier skill caveat called this 'overstated' — that was WRONG for Egypt. The breadth comes from the consumption/utilization principle, not a PE test.
withholding_tax_crossborder.impact: A $10,000 invoice nets $8,000 — immediate 20% cash hit if unpriced.
withholding_tax_crossborder.dtt: Treaties can cut the effective rate to ~5-15% or exempt PE-less business profits, BUT Ministerial Decree 771/2009 forbids applying the treaty rate at source: payer withholds full 20% upfront (Form 11, monthly); the non-resident files a refund claim (residency cert legalized by Egyptian consulate + beneficial-ownership + no-PE proof).
withholding_tax_crossborder.mitigation_gross_up: Global vendors refuse the refund hassle and enforce 'net of all taxes' clauses, forcing the Egyptian agency to gross up and absorb the 20%. When the agency is the FOREIGN provider billing an Egyptian client, insert your own gross-up clause so net remittance = invoice value.

social_insurance_2026.health_uhi_employer: 3.25% of GROSS wage — UNCAPPED (raises cost of senior talent)
social_insurance_2026.training_fund_employer: 0.25% of the minimum insurable wage per employee (restructured by Labour Law 14/2025; no longer a profit levy)
social_insurance_2026.worked_senior: Gross EGP 40,000/mo: pension capped -> employer 16,700x18.75% = 3,131.25, employee 16,700x11% = 1,837. Health uncapped on 40,000 -> employer 1,300, employee 400. Training ~0.25%x2,700 = 6.75. TOTAL employer burden ~EGP 4,438/mo (~11% of gross); employee deduction ~2,237/mo.

personal_income_tax_2026.note: Brackets apply to net taxable income AFTER the EGP 20,000 exemption and allowable social-insurance deductions. High earners lose access to lower brackets.

msme_simplified_turnover_tax.eligibility: Annual turnover up to EGP 20M; MUST be fully on e-invoicing AND e-receipt systems (lapse = retroactive 22.5% net-profit assessment).
msme_simplified_turnover_tax.why_it_matters: HUGE for a high-margin software/3D agency with minimal deductible COGS: a 1.5% gross-turnover tax can beat 22.5% on net profit by a wide margin. Model both and elect the cheaper. Also exemptions on dividends, capital gains on fixed-asset sales, and stamp duty.

currency_risk.trajectory_correction: Authoritative rate is ~52.17 (user-confirmed 8 Jun 2026). The research report's 47.95 figure (flagged 'Likely') was too strong and is REJECTED; the skill's original ~51.8 assumption was close. After the Mar 2024 float the EGP stabilized but kept a mild slide, sitting ~52.17 by mid-2026 — IMF EFF/RSF inflows, FDI, and tourism slowed but did not reverse the depreciation.
currency_risk.inflation_2026: IMF projection 11.8% avg; Central Bank of Egypt baseline 16.0% avg (energy/fiscal-consolidation driven).
currency_risk.arbitrage: Costs/payroll inflate 11-16% in EGP but are absorbed by USD revenue converting at a stable, favourable rate. Still BILL GLOBAL CLIENTS IN USD.
contract_protections: Currency Option Clause — pivot pricing to USD/EUR if FX deviates beyond a benchmark.
Indexation/Escalation — tie multi-year retainers to inflation indices (11-16%/yr).
Shortened review cycles — quarterly price reviews (mirrors Art. 47 Public Contracting Law).
Theory of Exceptional Circumstances (Civil Code) — a judge MAY adjust pricing after an unforeseeable general event; FX moves alone usually do NOT qualify as force majeure.

eor_note: Hiring via Employer of Record: premium global EORs charge 10-15% of gross salary (penalizes senior hires); regional flat-rate EORs (~EUR 199/employee/mo) give cost predictability.
